summary: Dashboards missing failover annotations during controlled failover test (add automation-driven markers)
description:
Requester: SRE/On-call

Context:
During the 2026-01-15 controlled regional failover (us-east → eu-west), the failover signal dashboards did not show timeline annotations for key automation actions (policy flip recommended/executed, rollback, hold-down timer activation, dedicated drain start/stop). This made it hard to align metric changes (5xx burn, tail latency, reachability probes, capacity headroom) with what the controller actually did.

Problem:
- Grafana/Datadog panels lacked vertical markers for:
  - failover_controller: decision computed (dry-run) vs executed
  - routing policy flips (primary/secondary region change)
  - rollback events and reasons (anti-flap / hold-down)
  - dedicated drain workflow milestones
- In the live #incidents thread, we relied on manual timestamp callouts, which were inconsistent and not searchable.

Impact:
- Slower triage during the game day (multiple minutes spent correlating logs + Slack timestamps).
- Higher risk of misattributing metric anomalies to routing vs client retry behavior.
- Makes post-test reporting and SLO review harder (timeline gaps).

Request:
Add automation-driven dashboard annotations that are emitted by the failover controller/audit stream and automatically rendered on the failover dashboards (and ideally in the incident timeline tooling).

Expected behavior:
When automation emits a failover event, an annotation appears on the "Failover Signals" and "Multi-region Availability" dashboards with:
- timestamp
- event_type (recommendation|execution|rollback|hold_down|approval_requested|approval_granted|drain_start|drain_complete)
- region_from / region_to (where applicable)
- reason (normalized string)
- actor (automation|oncall user)
- correlation ids (run_id, incident_id if present)

Notes/constraints:
- Avoid label/cardinality explosion (no tenant_id in annotations; use tier + route class).
- Must work in prod and staging.
- Should not require manual steps during game day (annotations must appear automatically within ~30s).

References:
- Game day results doc (timeline shows missing gaps around rollback)
- Failover event audit logs exist but are not surfaced in dashboards
- INT-1142 has the change-approval record; this is specifically observability/timeline UX

acceptance_criteria: Failover dashboards render automatic annotations for controller audit events within 30s of event emission (staging + prod).
Annotations include at minimum: event_type, region_from/region_to (if applicable), normalized reason, run_id/correlation id.
Dedicated drain milestones appear as annotations (drain_start, drain_complete) tied to the same run_id.
Annotation text is human-readable and consistent (no unbounded free-form reason strings).
No high-cardinality dimensions introduced (explicitly exclude tenant_id and request_id).
Runbook/game day checklist can reference: “Verify annotations present” as a pre-flight check.
